items.prompt:
In a design problem, the goals a solution must meet are called
A) constraints
B) criteria
C) materials
D) guesses

steps: Criteria are the goals for success.

items.prompt:
The limits a solution must stay within are called
A) criteria
B) constraints
C) rewards
D) colors

steps: Constraints are limits like materials, time, or cost.

items.prompt:
'Use only paper and tape' is a
A) criterion
B) constraint
C) reward
D) test result

steps: It limits the materials, so it is a constraint.

items.prompt:
Why define the criteria before building?
A) To slow down
B) So you know what success looks like and can test for it
C) To avoid testing
D) It does not matter
items.answer: B) So you know what success looks like and can test for it

steps: Clear criteria guide the design and allow testing.

items.prompt:
Which is a cost constraint?
A) The design must be blue
B) The design must cost less than five dollars
C) The design must hold 10 blocks
D) The design must be fun
items.answer: B) The design must cost less than five dollars

steps: A money limit is a cost constraint.

items.prompt:
'Finish in 30 minutes' is an example of a
A) criterion
B) time constraint
C) material
D) reward

steps: A time limit is a constraint.

items.prompt:
Which is a well-defined design problem?
A) Make something cool
B) Build the best thing ever
C) Build a shade that lowers the temperature by 5 degrees using only cardboard in one day
D) Do a good job
items.answer: C) Build a shade that lowers the temperature by 5 degrees using only cardboard in one day

steps: Only this one names a measurable criterion and clear constraints.

items.prompt:
A team must hold 10 blocks using at most 20 craft sticks. Which part is the criterion?
A) Use at most 20 craft sticks
B) Hold 10 blocks
C) Work in a group
D) Use craft sticks

steps: Holding 10 blocks is the goal for success; the stick limit is the constraint.
